title: Pounds and kilograms, inches and centimeters
blurb: Change pounds to kilograms and back with 2.2, inches to centimeters and back with 2.54, and handle heights and weights written in mixed units.
question: A patient is 5 ft 7 in tall and weighs 165 lb. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb and 1 in = 2.54 cm, what height and weight should go in an electronic record that uses centimeters and kilograms?

teach.h: Two bridges you must know by heart
teach.body: Formally, a conversion factor is a ratio of two equal quantities in different units: 1 kg = 2.2 lb (rounded from 2.2046) and 1 in = 2.54 cm (exact). Multiplying by it changes the unit but not the amount. In plain English: one memorized fact links pounds to kilograms, and one links inches to centimeters. Any other cross-system factor the HESI A2 needs (ounces to grams, miles to kilometers) is printed in the question.

head: Conversion
Value
On the exam
teach.caption: When the stem prints a factor, use exactly that number, even if you remember a more precise one.

teach.body: A kilogram is heavier than a pound, so a weight in kilograms is the SMALLER number: pounds to kilograms, divide by 2.2. An inch is longer than a centimeter, so a length in centimeters is the BIGGER number: inches to centimeters, multiply by 2.54. If unsure, write the factor as a fraction with the wanted unit on top: 154 lb × (1 kg / 2.2 lb) = 70 kg, and the pounds cancel.

rows.label: Why
values: A kg is the heavier unit
A lb is the lighter unit

teach.caption: Sense check: a person's weight in kilograms is always a smaller number than in pounds.
Pounds and centimeters are the "many small units" sides: going toward them, multiply.

items: 4.5 kg to lb: 4.5 × 2.2 = 9.9 lb. In pounds and ounces: 0.9 × 16 = 14.4, so about 9 lb 14 oz.
50.8 cm to in: 50.8 ÷ 2.54 = 20 in, which is 1 ft 8 in. Check: 20 × 2.54 = 50.8 cm.
7 lb 8 oz to kg: 8 oz = 0.5 lb, so 7.5 lb. 7.5 ÷ 2.2 = 3.41 kg (to the nearest hundredth).

teach.caption: A meter is a little longer than a yard (1 yd = 0.9144 m exactly).

teach.h: Scenario: Marcus updates an electronic record
teach.body: Marcus, a patient care tech applying to a radiography program, measures a patient at 5 ft 7 in and 165 lb, but the record takes centimeters and kilograms. Height: 5 × 12 + 7 = 67 in, and 67 × 2.54 = 170.18 cm. Weight: 165 ÷ 2.2 = 75 kg. Check: 75 × 2.2 = 165 lb. Had he multiplied by 2.2, he would have entered 363 kg, an obvious error a sense check catches.

teach.text: Multiply or divide? lb to kg is DIVIDE by 2.2; kg to lb is MULTIPLY. in to cm is MULTIPLY by 2.54; cm to in is DIVIDE. Also watch for 2.54 used on feet (convert feet to inches first), 5 ft 4 in read as 5.4 ft, and 0.9 lb read as 9 oz (a pound has 16 ounces).

items: Memorize: 1 kg = 2.2 lb; 1 in = 2.54 cm (so 1 ft = 30.48 cm); 16 oz = 1 lb; 12 in = 1 ft.
Change mixed units to one unit first (5 ft 6 in = 66 in; 7 lb 8 oz = 7.5 lb).
Ounce-to-gram and mile-to-kilometer factors come in the stem: use them exactly.
Sense check: kilograms are a smaller number than pounds; centimeters a bigger number than inches.

summary: You can now convert pounds and kilograms with 2.2 and inches and centimeters with 2.54 in either direction, and you know which way to go without guessing. You can also handle heights and weights in mixed units such as 5 ft 4 in or 7 lb 8 oz.

A.q: A patient weighs 187 lb. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the patient's weight in kilograms?
A.why: Pounds to kilograms: divide by 2.2. 187 ÷ 2.2 = 85 kg. Check: 85 × 2.2 = 187 lb.

whyNot.0: This multiplies by 2.2. A weight in kilograms must be a smaller number than in pounds.
whyNot.3: The division is right but the decimal point has slipped one place.

A.q: A wound measures 3.5 in long. What is its length in centimeters, to the nearest hundredth?

whyNot.0: This divides by 2.54. Centimeters are smaller than inches, so the number must get bigger.
whyNot.1: The decimal point has slipped one place to the right.
whyNot.2: This rounds the factor to 2.5; the exact factor is 2.54.

A.q: A patient weighs 54 kg. What is the patient's weight in pounds?
A.why: Kilograms to pounds: multiply by 2.2. 54 × 2.2 = 118.8 lb. Check: 118.8 ÷ 2.2 = 54 kg.

whyNot.0: This divides by 2.2; kilograms to pounds means multiplying.
whyNot.3: This multiplies by 2.54, the inches-to-centimeters factor.

B.q: A baby weighs 4.5 kg. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the baby's weight in pounds and ounces, to the nearest ounce?
B.why: 4.5 × 2.2 = 9.9 lb. Keep 9 lb and convert the 0.9 lb: 0.9 × 16 = 14.4, which rounds to 14 oz. So 9 lb 14 oz.

whyNot.0: This reads 0.9 lb as 9 oz. A pound has 16 ounces, so 0.9 lb is 14.4 oz.
whyNot.1: This divides by 2.2 (4.5 ÷ 2.2 is about 2.05 lb). kg to lb means multiply.
whyNot.3: This uses 12 oz per pound (0.9 × 12 = 10.8, about 11 oz).

B.q: A newborn's head circumference is 34.29 cm. What is this in inches?
B.why: Centimeters to inches: divide by 2.54. 34.29 ÷ 2.54 = 13.5 in. Check: 13.5 × 2.54 = 34.29 cm.

whyNot.0: This divides by 25.4, the millimeters in an inch, but the measurement is in centimeters.
whyNot.2: This divides by 2.2, the pounds-per-kilogram factor.
whyNot.3: This multiplies by 2.54; inches are larger, so the number must get smaller.

B.q: A nursing applicant is 5 ft 4 in tall. What is this height in centimeters, to the nearest hundredth?

whyNot.0: This reads 5 ft 4 in as 54 in (54 × 2.54 = 137.16).
whyNot.1: This reads 5 ft 4 in as 5.4 ft (64.8 in), but 4 in is 4/12 of a foot, not 0.4.
whyNot.2: This divides 64 by 2.54 instead of multiplying.

C.q: A patient weighed 92 kg at admission and 198 lb at discharge. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how did the patient's weight change?
C.why: Same units first: 198 ÷ 2.2 = 90 kg. 92 - 90 = 2, so the patient lost 2 kg. Check: 92 kg = 202.4 lb, and 202.4 - 198 = 4.4 lb = 2 kg.

whyNot.1: The discharge weight (90 kg) is lower than the admission weight (92 kg), so this is a loss.
whyNot.2: 4.4 is the loss in pounds (202.4 - 198); in kilograms it is 4.4 ÷ 2.2 = 2 kg.
whyNot.3: This divides the 2 kg loss by 2.2 a second time.

C.q: A wound measured 4 cm long on Monday and 1 1/2 in long on Friday. Using 1 in = 2.54 cm, by how many centimeters did it shrink?

whyNot.1: This subtracts 1.5 from 4 without changing the inches to centimeters.
whyNot.2: This divides 1.5 by 2.54 (0.59) instead of multiplying, then subtracts.
whyNot.3: This subtracts 4 - 1.5 = 2.5 with mixed units and then multiplies by 2.54.

C.q: A newborn weighs 8 lb 4 oz. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the weight in kilograms, to the nearest hundredth?
C.why: 4 oz = 4/16 = 0.25 lb, so the weight is 8.25 lb. 8.25 ÷ 2.2 = 3.75 kg.

whyNot.0: This converts the 8 lb (8 ÷ 2.2 = 3.64) and leaves out the 4 oz.
whyNot.2: This writes 8 lb 4 oz as 8.4 lb; 4 oz is 0.25 lb, not 0.4 lb.
whyNot.3: This multiplies 8.25 by 2.2; pounds to kilograms means dividing.

reteach.title: Think of exchanging currency
reteach.question: Changing dollars into another currency uses an exchange rate. How is a bridge factor like an exchange rate?

blocks.body: At a currency desk, the rate tells you how many units of one currency equal one unit of the other. Changing money does not change its value, only the label and the number. A conversion factor is an exchange rate for units: 1 in "buys" 2.54 cm, and 1 kg "buys" 2.2 lb. When you exchange into the smaller unit, you receive more of them; into the bigger unit, fewer.

blocks.text: Before you calculate, decide whether you should end up with more units or fewer. If your answer goes the other way, you multiplied when you should have divided.

explain.body: 1 in = 2.54 cm exactly, so 1 ft = 12 × 2.54 = 30.48 cm. 1 kg = 2.2 lb is the standard health-care factor.

test.q: How many centimeters are in 1 foot?

whyNot.0: 2.54 cm is one inch, not one foot.
whyNot.1: This divides 12 by 2.54 instead of multiplying.
whyNot.3: 25.4 is the number of millimeters in one inch.

explain.body: Put the unit you want on top. To turn kg into lb, multiply by (2.2 lb / 1 kg) so that kg cancels.

test.q: Which setup correctly converts 68 kg to pounds?
test.why: With pounds on top and kilograms on the bottom, kg cancels and the answer is in pounds: 68 × 2.2 = 149.6 lb.

whyNot.1: Kilograms are on top, so nothing cancels: this divides by 2.2.
whyNot.2: Dividing by the fraction is the same as dividing by 2.2, the wrong direction.
whyNot.3: This factor is false: 1 lb is not equal to 2.2 kg.

explain.body: For weight ounces to grams or miles to kilometers, the HESI A2 gives the factor. Use that exact number, and keep weight ounces (28 g) apart from fluid ounces (30 mL).

test.q: Using 1 oz = 28 g, about how many ounces is a 340 g package of pasta, to the nearest tenth?
test.why: Grams to ounces: 340 ÷ 28 = 12.14..., which rounds to 12.1 oz.

whyNot.1: This divides by 16, the ounces-per-pound factor, which does not convert grams.
whyNot.2: This divides by 30, the fluid-ounce factor for milliliters; weight ounces use 28 g.

explain.body: Turn mixed customary units into one unit before crossing systems: 1 ft 8 in = 12 + 8 = 20 in, then 20 × 2.54 = 50.8 cm.

test.q: A newborn is 1 ft 8 in long. What is the length in centimeters, to the nearest tenth?

whyNot.0: This reads 1 ft 8 in as 1.8 ft; 8 in is 8/12 of a foot.
whyNot.2: This converts the foot (30.48 cm) but adds the 8 in without converting them.
whyNot.3: This divides 20 by 2.54 instead of multiplying.
